paragraphs: Unless otherwise noted in this report, any description of "we," "us" or "our" includes Molson Coors Beverage Company ("MCBC" or the "Company"), principally a holding company, and its operating and non-operating subsidiaries included within its reporting segments. Our reporting segments include the Americas and EMEA&APAC. Unless otherwise indicated, information in this report is presented in USD and comparisons are to comparable prior periods. Our primary operating currencies, other than the USD, include the CAD, the GBP and our Central European operating currencies, such as the EUR, CZK, RON and RSD.

For more than two centuries, we have brewed beverages that unite people to celebrate all life's moments. From our core power brands, Coors Light, Miller Lite, Coors Banquet, Molson Canadian, Carling and Ožujsko, to our above premium brands, including Madrí Excepcional, Staropramen, Blue Moon Belgian White and Leinenkugel's Summer Shandy, to our value brands, like Miller High Life and Keystone Light, we produce many beloved and iconic beers. While our Company's history is rooted in beer, we offer a modern portfolio that expands beyond the beer aisle as well, including flavored beverages like Vizzy Hard Seltzer, spirits and non-alcoholic beverages. We also have partner brands, such as Simply Spiked, ZOA Energy, Fever-Tree, among others, through license, distribution, partnership and joint venture agreements. As a business, our ambition is to be the first choice for our people, our consumers and our customers, and our success depends on our ability to make our products available to meet a wide range of consumer segments and occasions.

Our primary founders, the Molson, Coors and Miller families date back over two centuries. Our commitment to producing the highest quality beers is a key part of our heritage and remains so to this day. Our brands are designed to appeal to a wide range of consumer tastes, styles and price preferences. Coors Brewing Company was incorporated in June 1913 under the laws of the state of Colorado. In October 2003, Coors Brewing Company merged with and into Adolph Coors Company, a Delaware corporation. In February 2005, Adolph Coors Company merged with Molson Inc. ("the Merger"). Upon completion of the Merger, Adolph Coors Company changed its name to Molson Coors Brewing Company. In 2008, Molson Coors Brewing Company and the former SABMiller plc formed the MillerCoors joint venture that combined their respective operations in the U.S. and Puerto Rico with Molson Coors Brewing Company maintaining a 42% share in the joint venture. In 2016, we acquired 100% of the outstanding equity and voting interests of MillerCoors, from SABMiller plc. In January 2020, we changed our name from Molson Coors Brewing Company to Molson Coors Beverage Company in connection with our expansion beyond the beer aisle.

The brewing industry has significantly evolved over the years to become an increasingly global and complex market as the consolidation of brewers globally has resulted in a small number of large global brewers representing the majority of the worldwide beer market. Although we believe consolidation among current major brewers has largely concluded, the current landscape primarily features smaller-scale acquisitions including exports, licensing and partnership arrangements. These activities continue to occur predominantly among the same global competitors that represent the majority of the market. While the majority of the market is represented by a small number of large global brewers, smaller local brewers continue to inhabit the market as consumers place value on locally-produced, regionally-sourced products.

The brewing industry is highly competitive and our portfolio of beers competes with numerous brands in all segments which are produced by international, national, regional and local brewers. Competitive factors impacting our business include, but are not limited to, brand recognition and loyalty, pricing, quality, advertising, marketing and promotional activity, packaging, product variety, and the ability to anticipate and respond to consumer tastes and preferences. We believe our brand portfolio gives us strong representation in all major beer categories. We are among the top five global brewers in the world. In the U.S. and Canada, we compete most directly with Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV ("ABI") and Constellation Brands, Inc., but we also compete with imports and other providers of craft beer and flavored malt beverages. In the European countries where we currently operate, our primary competitors are Heineken, Asahi, Carlsberg and ABI. Globally, our products also compete with other alcohol beverage categories, including wine, spirits as well as wine-based and spirits-based RTDs. Our products' competitive position is affected by consumer preferences between and among these other categories. Shifts between these beverage categories have resulted in a reduction in the beer segment's lead in the overall alcohol beverage market over the last decade.

Consumer preferences have continued to shift within the industry to above premium products, with volume growth in recent years seen in flavored malt beverages, imports and super premium portfolios. Further, consumers are expanding into spirits, particularly to spirits-based RTDs.

As the beer industry continues its diversification of its products to meet consumer demand with broadening preferences, we believe large global brewers are uniquely positioned to leverage the scale, depth of product portfolio and industry knowledge to continue to lead the market forward. Since 2019, we have made progress on our transformation journey to become a total beverage company, but given the fast-paced and evolving industry, we are focused on transforming even faster.

Under the leadership of our new Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"), effective October 1, 2025, we are continuing our journey to become a total beverage company and putting ourselves on a path to sustainable growth. We announced an Americas Restructuring Plan aimed at putting the right level of resources closer to our consumers and customers as we pursue a return to growth, both concentrating on all segments of our beer portfolio and expanding into adjacent categories, such as premium mixers, non-alcohol beverages and energy drinks. We aim to champion beer at every turn while building a portfolio that reflects evolving preferences. Our investments in technology, capabilities, partnerships and innovation are designed to support profitable growth and diversification, positioning our company for success today and in the future.

Our reporting segments include the Americas and EMEA&APAC. A separate operating team manages each segment and each segment manufactures, markets, distributes and sells beer as well as offers a modern and growing portfolio that expands beyond the beer aisle.

Our Americas segment consists of the production, importing, marketing, distribution and sales of our owned brands, partner brands and licensed brands in the U.S., Canada and various countries in Latin America. We currently operate nine primary breweries, three craft breweries and two container operations. The Americas segment also includes partnership arrangements with Brewers' Retail Inc. ("BRI") for the distribution of beer in Ontario, Canada, and Brewers' Distributor Ltd. ("BDL") for the distribution of beer in the western provinces of Canada. In addition, we have an agreement with Heineken that grants us the right to produce, import, market, distribute and sell certain Heineken products in Canada. We have authorizations from Red Tree Beverages, LLC that grant us the right to produce, market, advertise, promote, sell and distribute products bearing the Simply Spiked trademark in the U.S. and Canada, as well as the Topo Chico Hard Seltzer trademark in the U.S. In addition, we have agreements to brew, package and ship products for The Yuengling Company ("TYC") in the U.S. and we have a license agreement to import, produce, market, advertise, promote, sell and distribute Fever-Tree products in the U.S.

Our EMEA&APAC segment consists of the production, marketing and sales of our owned brands, partner brands and licensed brands in Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Montenegro, the Republic of Ireland, Romania, Serbia, the U.K., various other European countries and certain countries within the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific regions. We currently operate ten primary breweries, three craft breweries and one cidery. The majority of our EMEA&APAC segment sales are in the U.K., Croatia, Romania and the Czech Republic, with the U.K. representing over 55% of the segment's net sales in 2025.

Our EMEA&APAC segment includes the sale of factored brands in the U.K. which occurs when we distribute beer, wine, spirits and other products owned and produced by other companies to the on-premise channel, such as bars and restaurants. Sales from factored brands are included in our net sales and cost of goods sold when ultimately sold.

We also have certain activity that is not allocated to our segments, which is reflected in "Unallocated". Specifically, Unallocated primarily includes certain financing-related activities such as interest expense and interest income, as well as foreign exchange gains and losses on intercompany balances. Unallocated activity also includes the unrealized changes in fair value on our commodity swaps not designated in hedging relationships recorded within cost of goods sold, which are later reclassified when realized to the segment in which the underlying exposure resides. Additionally, only the service cost component of net periodic pension and OPEB cost is reported within each operating segment. Meanwhile, all other components remain in Unallocated.

Total industry volume is sensitive to factors such as weather, holidays and certain occasions including major broadcasted or streamed sporting events. Weather conditions consisting of high temperatures and extended periods of warm and dry weather favor increased consumption of our products, while unseasonably cool or wet weather, especially during the summer months, adversely affects our sales volumes and net sales. Consumption of beer is seasonal with approximately 40% of financial volume occurring during the months of May through August in both the Americas and EMEA&APAC segments.

headings: Risks Related to our Company and Operations
Risks Related to Our Indebtedness, Capital Structure and Financial Condition
paragraphs: Investing in our Company involves risk. Investors should carefully consider the following risk factors and the other information contained within this report. The risks set forth below are those that management believes are most likely to have a material adverse effect on us. Investors are encouraged to read each risk factor as related and interconnected to the other risk factors set forth in this section. However, the risks set forth below are not a comprehensive description of the risks facing our Company. We may also be subject to other risks or uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial but may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations in future periods. Investors should not interpret the disclosure of any risk factor to imply that the risk has not already materialized. If the following risks or uncertainties, individually or in combination, actually occur, they may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial conditions, results of operations or prospects. See also "Cautionary Statement Pursuant to Safe Harbor Provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995."

The global beer industry and the broader alcohol industry are constantly evolving and our position within these industries and the success of our products in our markets may fundamentally change. If we do not successfully transform along with the evolving industries, market dynamics and consumer preferences, our business and financial results could be materially adversely affected. The brewing industry has significantly evolved over the years becoming an increasingly consolidated global beer market. For many years, the industry operated primarily on local presence with modest international expansion achieved through export, license and partnership arrangements. In contrast, it has now become increasingly complex and competitive as the consolidation of brewers has resulted in fewer major market participants. As a result, the markets in which we operate, particularly the more mature markets, like the U.S., Canada and the U.K., may evolve at a disadvantage to our current market position. Ongoing evolution in certain of our beer markets, together with emerging changes in consumer preferences, have resulted in a significant increase in market entrants, new and innovative products, consumer choices and market competition.

Our Coors Light and Miller Lite brands in the Americas represented approximately 55% of segment net sales in 2025 while, Carling, Staropramen, Coors, Madrí Excepcional, Ožujsko, and Bergenbier brands in EMEA&APAC represented approximately 45% of segment net sales in 2025, with several of our other brands representing a significant share of their respective markets. Therefore, continued volatility in these markets could disproportionately impact the performance of these brands. Consequently, any material shift in consumer preferences away from these brands, or from the categories in which they compete, could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results.

Furthermore, the broader alcohol industry is also experiencing a shift in consumer drinking preferences and behaviors due to, among others, downturns in economic conditions or perceived value, changing demographics and taste preferences, such as the expansion in above premium products, specifically flavored malt beverages, RTDs, spirit-based beverages, cider and other similar beverages, as well as a shift toward non-alcoholic beverages, health and wellness trends (including the use of glucagon-like peptide (GLP-1) agonists), as well as changes in consumers' perception of our brands and the brands of our competitors. If we are unsuccessful in evolving with, and navigating through, these changes to the markets in which we operate, there could be a material adverse effect on our business and financial results. If our competitors are able to respond more quickly to the evolving trends within beverage categories, or if our new products in these categories are not successful, our business and financial results may be adversely impacted.

Our restructuring activities may not be successful and the estimated costs associated with such activities may be more than expected, and our restructuring activities may adversely impact employee hiring and retention. On October 20, 2025, we announced a corporate restructuring plan, the Americas Restructuring Plan, designed to create a leaner, more agile Americas organization while advancing our ability to reinvest in our business and position us for future growth. The restructuring involved the elimination of salaried positions across our Americas segment during the fourth quarter of 2025. The implementation of this plan may be disruptive to our operations, result in higher than anticipated restructuring charges, including severance and related costs, and otherwise adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition, and may not generate the expected savings or other benefits intended by management. Additional risks associated with the continuing impact of the restructuring activities include employee attrition, the ability to hire new employees in the future, diversion of management attention, and adverse effects on employee morale. In addition, our ability to complete this plan and achieve the anticipated benefits from it within the expected time frame, or at all, is subject to management's estimates and assumptions and may vary materially from our expectations, including as a result of factors that are beyond our control. If we do not realize the expected benefits of this plan on a timely basis, or at all, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected. Furthermore, following completion of this plan, our business may not be more efficient or effective than prior to the implementation of such plan.

Competition and other factors in our markets could require us to adjust prices or increase capital and other expenditures or cause us to lose sales volume, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results. In many of our markets, our primary competitors may have greater financial, marketing, production and distribution resources than we do, and may be more diverse in terms of their geographies and brand portfolios. We compete with other beer and beverage companies not only for consumer acceptance and loyalty, but also for shelf, refrigerator and tap space in retail establishments and for marketing focus by our distributors and customers, most of which also distribute and sell other beers and beverage products. If we do not successfully transform along with the evolving industry, market dynamics and consumer preferences, our business and financial results could be materially adversely affected. Furthermore, our competitors may respond to industry and economic conditions and shifts in consumer behaviors more rapidly or effectively than we do. In order for us to remain competitive, we will need to continue to quickly and correctly adopt digital technologies, build analytical capabilities and scale brand expense investment levels, which our competitors may be able to achieve faster and with more resources. In all of the markets in which we operate, aggressive marketing strategies, such as reduced pricing, brand positioning, and increased capital or other investments by these competitors could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results.

Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") in this Annual Report on Form 10-K is provided to assist in understanding our Company, operations and current business environment and should be considered a supplement to, and read in conjunction with, the accompanying audited consolidated financial statements and notes included within Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, as well as the discussion of our business and related risk factors in Part I—Item 1 Business and Part I—Item 1A Risk Factors, respectively. See also "Cautionary Statement Pursuant to Safe Harbor Provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995."

A discussion related to the results of operations and changes in financial condition for 2024 compared to 2023 has been omitted from this report, but may be found in Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in our fiscal 2024 Form 10-K, filed with the SEC on February 18, 2025, which is available free of charge on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov and our corporate website at www.molsoncoors.com. The information provided on our website (or any other website referred to in this report) is not part of this report and is not incorporated by reference as part of this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, (a) all $ amounts are in USD, (b) comparisons are to comparable prior periods and (c) 2025, 2024 and 2023 refers to the 12 months ended December 31, 2025, December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively.

Our industry is experiencing, and we expect will continue to experience, increased consumer and economic uncertainty due to volatility in the global macroeconomic environment including global trade policies and other geopolitical events with potential resulting impacts on economic growth, consumer confidence, inflation and currencies and their exchange rates. In addition, the associated impacts of the macroeconomic environment on the beer industry in the U.S. has resulted in heightened competitive activity and associated reduction in market share of our products in certain segments. The magnitude of the resulting impacts on our business are dependent on the evolution of the global macroeconomic environment and the competitive landscape, including whether market share losses are sustained. The economic and competitive pressures, including the impact of tariffs, on our Company and our consumers' consumption behavior and preferences have negatively impacted, and may continue to negatively impact, our results of operations during this volatile period. For example, tariff announcements in the U.S. in the second quarter of 2025 have indirectly caused the price of the premium on aluminum in the U.S., known as the Midwest Premium, to spike and remain elevated which resulted in an approximate $35 million unfavorable impact on our results for the year ended December 31, 2025 and is expected to continue to adversely impact our results of operations. While our hedging program can help mitigate some of the volatility, the opaque pricing and limited liquidity of the Midwest Premium can make hedging this exposure costly. In addition to impacting the prices of raw materials, a constant or periodic change in the Midwest Premium may decrease our profit margins or we may pass on the increased costs to our consumers which could in turn result in the loss of sales if the end consumer is not willing to pay the increased price. We plan to continue to evaluate and implement strategies which are designed to help mitigate the impact on our business, consolidated results of operations and financial condition while continuing to support our long-term strategic growth and capital allocation priorities.

On April 12, 2025, Gavin D.K. Hattersley, the then President and CEO of our Company and a then member of the Board, informed our Company and the Board that he intended to retire from our Company and as a member of the Board, in each case, by December 31, 2025.

On September 19, 2025, the Board appointed Rahul Goyal as our Company's President and CEO and member of the Board effective, in each case, as of October 1, 2025, following the retirement of Gavin D.K. Hattersley from those same positions immediately prior to such appointments. Gavin D.K. Hattersley remained employed by our Company in an advisory role to assist in the transition until December 31, 2025.

On September 26, 2024, we purchased annuity contracts for two of our Canadian pension plans. As a result, on September 30, 2024, we remeasured both pension plans and recorded a total settlement loss of $34.0 million to other pension and postretirement benefit (costs), net in our consolidated statements of operations during the third quarter of 2024. See Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 11, "Employee Retirement Plans and Postretirement Benefits" and Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 15, "Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss)" for further information.

During March 2024, our partner in Cobra Beer Partnership, Ltd. ("CBPL") exercised a put option under our partnership agreement which required us to acquire the remaining 49.9% ownership interest. We adjusted the NCI by $34.5 million to our best estimate of the redemption value that existed at the time of the put option exercise by increasing net income attributable to noncontrolling interests and decreasing our net income attributable to MCBC. In addition, we received the final determination of the redemption value in October 2024 and as the transaction was considered mandatorily redeemable, we recorded an adjustment of $45.8 million to interest expense in the EMEA&APAC segment during the third quarter of 2024. The transaction was finalized on October 21, 2024, resulting in a cash payment of $89 million which was recorded as a cash outflow from financing activities.

On October 20, 2025, we announced an Americas Restructuring Plan designed to create a leaner, more agile Americas segment while advancing our ability to reinvest in the business and position our Company for future growth. The plan resulted in charges of $28.7 million, primarily related to severance payments and post-employment benefits, recorded to other operating income (expense), net in our consolidated statements of operations during the year ended December 31, 2025. The remaining charges, predominantly employee-related charges, for the Americas Restructuring Plan are expected to be recorded during the year ended December 31, 2026 and total restructuring charges are expected to be at the low end of the previously communicated range of $35 million to $50 million at approximately $35 million.

During the third quarter of 2025, we recorded a partial goodwill impairment charge of $3,645.7 million to goodwill impairment in our consolidated statement of operations related to our Americas reporting unit. See Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 6, "Goodwill and Intangible Assets" for further information.

During the third quarter of 2025, we recorded a full impairment charge of $75.3 million related to our Blue Run Spirits definite-lived intangible asset within other operating income (expense), net in our consolidated statements of operations. See Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 6, "Goodwill and Intangible Assets" for further information.

During the first quarter of 2025, we obtained exclusive rights via a license agreement to import, produce, market, advertise, promote, sell and distribute Fever-Tree products in the U.S. In connection with this agreement, we acquired the shares of the Fevertree USA, Inc. entity, with the immaterial acquisition accounted for as a business combination and consideration allocated primarily to working capital balances. The acquisition is aligned with our strategy to expand beyond the beer aisle.

On October 31, 2024, we further increased our investment in ZOA bringing our ownership interest to 51%. Upon conversion from equity method accounting to consolidation accounting, we recognized a gain of $77.9 million in other operating income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. See Part II—Item 8 Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 3, "Investments" for further information.

paragraphs: 除非本報告另有說明，任何有關「我們」、「我們」或「我們」的描述均包含 Molson Coors Beverage Company（「MCBC」或「本公司」），主要為一控股公司，及其營運與非營運子公司，包含於其應報告分部內。我們的應報告分部包括美洲與 EMEA&APAC。除非另有說明，本報告資訊以美元為單位呈現，並與可比較的前一時期進行比較。我們的主要營運貨幣，除美元外，包括加元、英鎊以及我們的中歐營運貨幣，例如歐元、捷克克朗、羅馬尼亞列伊與塞爾維亞第納爾。

在超過兩個世紀的時間裡，我們製造的飲料讓人們團結在一起，慶祝人生中的每一個時刻。從我們的核心強勢品牌，包括 Coors Light、Miller Lite、Coors Banquet、Molson Canadian、Carling 和 Ožujsko，到我們的高階精品品牌，包括 Madrí Excepcional、Staropramen、Blue Moon Belgian White 和 Leinenkugel's Summer Shandy，再到我們的價值型品牌，例如 Miller High Life 和 Keystone Light，我們製造許多受愛戴且具有代表性的啤酒。雖然我們公司的歷史根植於啤酒，但我們提供現代化的產品組合，擴展至啤酒架以外的領域，包括風味飲料如 Vizzy Hard Seltzer、烈酒與非酒精飲料。我們也透過授權、分銷、合作與合資協議擁有合作品牌，例如 Simply Spiked、ZOA Energy、Fever-Tree 等。作為一家企業，我們的目標是成為我們員工、消費者與客戶的首選，而我們的成功取決於我們能否讓產品可供不同消費羣體與場合使用。

我們的主要創始家族，Molson、Coors 與 Miller 家族，歷史可追溯至兩個世紀以上。我們致力於製造最高品質啤酒的承諾，是我們的遺產，至今依然如此。我們的品牌設計用以吸引廣泛的消費者口味、風格與價格偏好。Coors Brewing Company 於 1913 年 6 月根據科羅拉多州法律成立。2003 年 10 月，Coors Brewing Company 合併進 Adolph Coors Company，一間德拉華州公司。2005 年 2 月，Adolph Coors Company 合併進 Molson Inc.（「合併」）。合併完成後，Adolph Coors Company 更名為 Molson Coors Brewing Company。2008 年，Molson Coors Brewing Company 與前 SABMiller plc 形成 MillerCoors 合資企業，整合其在美國與波多黎各的營運，Molson Coors Brewing Company 保留合資企業 42% 的股份。2016 年，我們取得 MillerCoors 全部已發行股權與投票權，來自 SABMiller plc。2020 年 1 月，我們將公司名稱從 Molson Coors Brewing Company 改為 Molson Coors Beverage Company，以配合我們擴展至啤酒架以外的業務。

啤酒產業在過去幾年已大幅演進，成為一個越來越全球化與複雜的市場，隨著全球釀酒商的併購，導致僅有少數大型全球釀酒商代表全球啤酒市場的絕大多數。雖然我們認為目前主要釀酒商的併購已大致完成，但目前市場主要特徵為小型規模的收購，包括出口、授權與合作安排。這些活動持續主要發生在代表市場絕大多數的相同全球競爭對手之間。雖然市場絕大多數由少數大型全球釀酒商代表，但小型地方釀酒商仍持續存在於市場中，因為消費者重視本地製造、地區來源的產品。

啤酒產業競爭激烈，我們的啤酒組合與眾多品牌在所有市場段位競爭，這些品牌由國際、國家、區域與地方釀酒商製造。影響我們業務的競爭因素包括但不限於品牌知名度與忠誠度、價格、品質、廣告、行銷與促銷活動、包裝、產品種類，以及預測與回應消費者口味與偏好的能力。我們認為我們的品牌組合使我們在所有主要啤酒類別中擁有強大的代表性。我們是全球前五大釀酒商之一。在美國與加拿大，我們最直接的競爭對手為 Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV（「ABI」）與 Constellation Brands, Inc.，但我們也與進口酒與其他精釀啤酒與風味麥芽飲料供應商競爭。在目前我們經營的歐洲國家，我們的主要競爭對手為 Heineken、Asahi、Carlsberg 與 ABI。在全球範圍內，我們的產品也與其他酒精飲料類別競爭，包括葡萄酒、烈酒以及基於葡萄酒與烈酒的 RTDs。我們產品的競爭地位受到消費者在這些其他類別之間偏好的影響。這些飲料類別之間的轉移，導致過去十年啤酒類別在整體酒精飲料市場中的領導地位有所下降。
消費者偏好持續在產業內轉向高階精品產品，近年來風味麥芽飲料、進口酒與超級精品組合的銷售量有所成長。此外，消費者正擴展至烈酒，特別是基於烈酒的 RTDs。
隨著啤酒產業持續其產品多元化，以符合消費者需求與廣泛的偏好，我們認為大型全球釀酒商獨特地處於優勢，能利用規模、產品組合深度與產業知識，持續領導市場前進。自 2019 年以來，我們在轉型成為總體飲料公司的旅程上已取得進展，但考慮到產業快速變動且持續演進，我們正專注於更快地轉型。

在新任首席執行長（「CEO」）領導下，自 2025 年 10 月 1 日起，我們持續進行成為總體飲料公司的旅程，並為可持續成長奠定基礎。我們宣佈了一項美洲重整計畫，旨在將適當的資源更接近消費者與客戶，以追求成長回歸，同時專注於我們啤酒組合的所有市場段位，並擴展至相關類別，例如高階混合飲料、非酒精飲料與能量飲料。我們旨在在每一步驟中推廣啤酒，同時建立反映消費者偏好的產品組合。我們在科技、能力、合作夥伴與創新上的投資，旨在支持獲利成長與多元化，為我們今日與未來的成功奠定基礎。
本公司應報告分部包括美洲與EMEA&APAC。每個分部由獨立的營運團隊管理，每個分部製造、行銷、配送與銷售啤酒，並提供現代化且持續成長的產品組合，其範圍已超越啤酒區隔。

本公司美洲分部包含在美國、加拿大與拉丁美洲多個國家生產、進口、行銷、配送與銷售本公司自有品牌、合作品牌與授權品牌的業務。目前本公司運作九座主要啤酒廠、三座精釀啤酒廠與兩座容器製造設施。美洲分部亦包含與Brewers' Retail Inc. ("BRI")的合作關係，用於加拿大安大略省的啤酒配送，以及與Brewers' Distributor Ltd. ("BDL")的合作關係，用於加拿大西部省份的啤酒配送。此外，本公司與Heineken有協議，賦予本公司在加拿大生產、進口、行銷、配送與銷售特定Heineken產品之權利。本公司已取得Red Tree Beverages, LLC的授權，賦予本公司在美國與加拿大生產、行銷、宣傳、推廣、銷售與配送標有Simply Spiked商標產品之權利，以及在美國標有Topo Chico Hard Seltzer商標產品之權利。此外，本公司與The Yuengling Company ("TYC")有協議，用於在美國製造、包裝與運送產品，並與Fever-Tree有進口、生產、行銷、宣傳、推廣、銷售與配送產品的授權協議，適用於美國。

本公司EMEA&APAC分部包含在保加利亞、克羅地亞、捷克共和國、匈牙利、蒙特內哥羅、愛爾蘭共和國、羅馬尼亞、塞爾維亞、英國、其他歐洲國家以及中東、非洲與亞太地區部分國家生產、行銷與銷售本公司自有品牌、合作品牌與授權品牌的業務。目前本公司運作十座主要啤酒廠、三座精釀啤酒廠與一座果酒廠。本公司EMEA&AP,AC分部的銷售主要集中於英國、克羅地亞、羅馬尼亞與捷克共和國，其中英國在2025年代表該分部淨銷售額的逾55%。
本公司EMEA&APAC分部包含在英國銷售經因素化的品牌，此情形發生於本公司將其他公司所擁有與生產的啤酒、葡萄酒、烈酒及其他產品配送至現場銷售通路（如酒吧與餐廳）時。經因素化的品牌銷售額包含於本公司淨銷售額與銷售成本中，當這些產品最終銷售時。
本公司亦有部分活動未歸屬於任何分部，反映於"未歸屬"項目。具體而言，未歸屬項目主要包含與融資相關的活動，如利息支出與利息收入，以及因公司間餘額產生的外匯收益與損失。未歸屬活動亦包含未實現的商譽期貨合約公允價值變動，這些變動記錄於成本中，並在實現時重新歸類至相關分部。同時，僅淨定期退休金與OPEB成本的服務成本部分會計入各營運分部，其他部分則維持於未歸屬項目。
總體行業銷售量對天氣、節日及特定場合（如重大廣播或串流體育賽事）等因素較為敏感。高溫與持續乾燥暖和的天氣條件有利於增加本公司產品的消費量，而異常寒冷或潮濕的天氣，特別是在夏季，則會不利於本公司銷售量與淨銷售額。啤酒消費具有季節性，約40%的財務銷售量發生在美洲與EMEA&APAC分部的5月至8月間。

paragraphs: 超過兩百年來，我們製造的飲料讓人們團結在一起，慶祝人生中所有的時刻。從我們的核心主力品牌 Coors Light、Miller Lite、Coors Banquet、Molson Canadian、Carling 和 Ožujsko，到我們的高階 premium 品牌，包括 Madrí Excepcional、Staropramen、Blue Moon Belgian White 和 Leinenkugel's Summer Shandy，再到我們的價值型品牌如 Miller High Life 和 Keystone Light，我們製造許多受歡迎且具有代表性的啤酒。雖然我們的公司歷史根植於啤酒，但我們的現代產品組合已擴展至啤酒架以外的領域，包括風味飲料如 Vizzy Hard Seltzer、酒類和非酒精飲料。我們也與 Simply Spiked、ZOA Energy、Fever-Tree 等品牌合作，透過授權、分銷、合作及合資協議等方式。作為一家企業，我們的願景是成為員工、消費者和客戶的首選，而我們的成功取決於我們能否讓產品供應給廣泛的消費者羣體和場合。
本年度報告 10-K 中的「管理層討論與分析（MD&A）」部分，旨在協助瞭解本公司、營運狀況與當前商業環境，應與附屬的經審計合併財務報表及附註，以及 Part II—Item 8 財務報表與補充資料，以及 Part I—Item 1 商業與 Part I—Item 1A 風險因素的討論一併閱讀。請參閱「根據 1995 年私人證券訴訟改革法案安全港條款的警示聲明」。

關於 2024 年營運結果與財務狀況變動的討論，已從本報告中省略，但可於 Part II, Item 7 找到。此部分為我們財務年度 2024 的 10-K 報告，於 2025 年 2 月 18 日提交至 SEC，並可在 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 及本公司網站 www.molsoncoors.com 免費取得。本網站（或本報告中提及的任何其他網站）的資訊並非本報告的一部分，亦未被納入本報告的參考內容。
除非另有說明，(a) 所有金額均以美元計算，(b) 比較為與可比的前一時期，(c) 2025、2024 和 2023 係指 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2023 年 12 月 31 日的 12 個月期間。

我們的產業正經歷，且預期將持續經歷，因全球總體經濟環境波動所導致的消費者與經濟不確定性，包括全球貿易政策及其他地緣政治事件，可能對經濟成長、消費者信心、通貨膨脹及貨幣與匯率產生影響。此外，總體經濟環境對美國啤酒產業的影響，已導致某些市場段落中我們產品的市場佔有率下降。對我們業務產生的影響程度，取決於全球總體經濟環境與競爭態勢的演變，包括市場佔有率的損失是否持續。經濟與競爭壓力，包括關稅的影響，已對本公司及消費者消費行為與偏好產生負面影響，並可能持續產生負面影響。例如，2025 年第二季美國的關稅公告，間接導致美國的鋁合金 premium 價格上漲並維持在高位，這導致我們 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年結果產生約 3500 萬美元的不利影響，且預期將持續對我們的營運結果產生負面影響。雖然我們的對沖計畫可以緩解部分波動，但 Midwest Premium 的價格不透明與流動性有限，可能使對沖此風險的成本高昂。除了影響原材料價格，Midwest Premium 的持續或週期性變動可能降低我們的毛利率，或我們可能將增加的成本轉嫁給消費者，這可能導致銷售量減少，如果最終消費者不願支付更高的價格。我們計畫持續評估並實施策略，以幫助緩解對我們業務、合併營運結果與財務狀況的影響，同時繼續支持我們的長期戰略成長與資本配置優先事項。
2025 年 4 月 12 日，Gavin D.K. Hattersley，當時本公司董事長兼首席執行長，並為董事會成員，通知本公司與董事會，他預計將於 2025 年 12 月 31 日前從本公司及董事會退休。
2025 年 9 月 19 日，董事會任命 Rahul Goyal 為本公司董事長兼首席執行長及董事會成員，自 2025 年 10 月 1 日起生效，此為 Gavin D.K. Hattersley 從相同職位退休後立即進行的任命。Gavin D.K. Hattersley 在此任命前繼續擔任本公司顧問職務，協助過渡，直至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。

2024 年 9 月 26 日，我們為兩個加拿大的退休金計畫購買了年金契約。因此，於 2024 年 9 月 30 日，我們重新衡量了這兩個退休金計畫，並在 2024 年第三季的合併營運結果中，記錄了總計 3400 萬美元的退休金計畫結清損失，歸類於其他退休金及退休後福利（費用），淨額。請參閱 Part II—Item 8 財務報表與補充資料，附註 11，「員工退休金計畫與退休後福利」以及 Part II—Item 8 財務報表與補充資料，附註 15，「累計其他綜合損益（損失）」以取得更多資訊。

2024年3月，我們在Cobra Beer Partnership, Ltd. ("CBPL") 的合作夥伴行使了根據合作協議的賣回選擇權，要求我們取得剩餘的49.9%股權。我們調整了非控制性權益（NCI），將其增加34.5百萬美元，以反映當時賣回選擇權行使時的現金紅利價值最佳估計，同時提高歸屬於非控制性權益的淨收入，並降低歸屬於MCBC的淨收入。此外，我們在2024年10月收到最終的現金紅利價值決定，因該交易被視為強制贖回，我們在2024年第三季EMEA&APAC應報告分部的財務報表中，將利息費用調整了45.8百萬美元。該交易於2024年10月21日完成，導致現金支付89百萬美元，此筆金額已記入籌資活動的現金流出。

2025年10月20日，我們宣佈了一項美洲區重整計畫，旨在建立一個更精簡、更具彈性的美洲區，同時提升我們重投資業務並為未來成長做準備的能力。該計畫導致了28.7百萬美元的費用，主要與遣散費及離職後福利相關，記入合併財務報表中的其他營運收入（費用），淨額。美洲區重整計畫的剩餘費用，主要是與員工相關的費用，預計於2026年12月31日財務年度內記入，總體重整費用預計將在先前通報的35百萬至50百萬美元範圍內，約為35百萬美元。
在2025年第三季，我們在合併財務報表中，針對美洲區應報告分部的商譽，記錄了一筆部分商譽減損費用，金額為3,645.7百萬美元，記入商譽減損。有關進一步資訊，請參閱第二部分—第8項財務報表及補充資料，附註6，"商譽與無形資產"。
在2025年第三季，我們在合併財務報表中的其他營運收入（費用），淨額中，針對Blue Run Spirits的有限壽命無形資產，記錄了一筆完整的減損費用，金額為75.3百萬美元。有關進一步資訊，請參閱第二部分—第8項財務報表及補充資料，附註6，"商譽與無形資產"。
2025年第一季，我們透過許可協議取得獨家權利，進口、生產、行銷、宣傳、推廣、銷售及分銷Fever-Tree產品於美國。根據此協議，我們取得了Fevertree USA, Inc.實體的股權，此無重大性質的取得被視為企業合併，並將考慮主要分配至營運資金的餘額。此取得與我們擴展至啤酒架以外領域的戰略一致。
2024年10月31日，我們進一步增加對ZOA的投資，使我們的股權比例達到51%。在從權益法會計轉為合併會計時，我們在合併財務報表中確認了77.9百萬美元的收益，記入其他營運收入（費用），淨額。有關進一步資訊，請參閱第二部分—第8項財務報表及補充資料，附註3，"投資"。

{'Risks Related to Our Indebtedness, Capital Structure and Financial Condition': '與我們之負債、資本結構及財務狀況相關之風險'}
paragraphs: 投資本公司涉及風險。投資人應仔細考慮下列風險因素及本報告中所包含的其他資訊。下列所列風險是管理階層認為最可能對我們造成重大不利影響的風險。投資人應閱讀每一個風險因素，並理解其與本節所列其他風險因素之間的關聯性。然而，下列所列風險並非對本公司所面臨風險的完整說明。我們也可能面臨其他未被我們目前知悉或認為不重要，但可能對我們未來營運、財務狀況或營業成果造成重大不利影響的風險或不確定性。投資人不應將任何風險因素的揭露解釋為表示該風險已經實現。如果上述風險或不確定性，單獨或共同發生，可能會對我們的營運、財務狀況、營業成果或前景造成重大不利影響。請參閱「根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案安全港條款的警示聲明。」

全球啤酒產業與更廣泛的酒精產業持續演化，我們在這些產業中的地位以及我們產品在市場上的成功可能發生根本性的改變。如果我們無法成功適應這些演化中的產業、市場動態與消費者偏好，我們的營運與財務結果可能受到重大不利影響。啤酒產業在過去幾年已大幅演化，成為一個日益集中化的全球啤酒市場。在許多年間，產業主要以當地存在為主，國際擴張則透過出口、授權與合作安排實現。相反地，目前產業已變得更加複雜且競爭激烈，由於釀酒廠的併購導致主要市場參與者減少。因此，我們所處的市場，特別是較成熟的市場，如美國、加拿大與英國，可能以不利於我們現有市場地位的方式演化。我們部分啤酒市場的持續演化，加上消費者偏好的新興變化，已導致市場進入口增加、新穎產品、消費者選擇與市場競爭顯著增加。

我們在美洲地區的Coors Light與Miller Lite品牌，於2025年代表約55%的應報告分部淨銷售額；而在EMEA&APAC地區的Carling、Staropramen、Coors、Madrí Excepcional、Ožujsko與Bergenbier品牌，於2025年代表約45%的應報告分部淨銷售額，而我們的其他幾個品牌則在各自市場中佔有顯著的份額。因此，這些市場的持續波動可能對這些品牌的表現造成不成比例的影響。因此，任何對這些品牌或其競爭類別的消費者偏好大幅轉移，都可能對我們的營運與財務結果造成重大不利影響。

此外，更廣泛的酒精產業也正經歷消費者飲酒偏好與行為的轉變，原因包括經濟條件惡化或 perceived value 的變化、人口結構的改變與口味偏好，例如高於 premium 產品的擴張，特別是風味麥芽飲料、即飲酒（RTDs）、酒精基飲料、蘋果汁及其他類似飲料，以及朝向非酒精飲料、健康與 wellness 趨勢（包括使用類 GLP-1 腎上腺素激動劑）的轉變，以及消費者對我們品牌與競爭對手品牌的看法改變。如果我們無法成功適應並應對這些市場的變化，可能會對我們的營運與財務結果造成重大不利影響。如果競爭對手能更快對飲料類別中的趨勢做出反應，或我們在這些類別中的新產品未能成功，我們的營運與財務結果可能受到不利影響。

我們的重整活動可能無法成功，與此活動相關的預估成本可能高於預期，且重整活動可能對員工的招聘與留任造成不利影響。2025年10月20日，我們宣佈了一項企業重整計畫，即美洲地區重整計畫，旨在建立一個更精簡、更具靈活性的美洲組織，同時提升我們重新投資業務與為未來成長做準備的能力。此重整計畫包括在2025年第四季內，於美洲地區部門內消除若干薪資職位。此計畫的實施可能對我們的營運造成幹擾，導致高於預期的重整費用，包括解僱與相關成本，並可能對我們的營業成果與財務狀況造成不利影響，且可能無法產生管理階層預期的節省或其他效益。與此重整活動持續影響相關的其他風險包括員工流失、未來招聘新員工的能力、管理階層注意力的分散，以及對員工士氣的負面影響。此外，我們完成此計畫並在預期時間內實現預期效益的能力，或是否能實現，取決於管理階層的預估與假設，且可能與我們的預期有重大差異，包括因不可控制因素所致。如果我們未能在預期時間內或根本無法實現此計畫的預期效益，我們的營運、營業成果與財務狀況可能受到重大不利影響。此外，在完成此計畫後，我們的營運可能不會比實施此計畫前更有效率或更有效。

我們市場中的競爭及其他因素可能導致我們必須調整價格或增加資本及其他支出，或導致我們失去銷售量，任何一種情況都可能對我們的營運與財務結果造成重大不利影響。在許多我們所處的市場中，我們的主要競爭對手可能擁有比我們更強的財務、行銷、生產與分銷資源，且他們在地理範圍與品牌組合上可能更加多元。我們不僅與其他啤酒與飲料公司競爭消費者接受度與忠誠度，還與他們競爭零售場所的架位、冷櫃與吧檯空間，以及我們的經銷商與客戶的行銷重點，而這些經銷商與客戶也分銷與銷售其他啤酒與飲料產品。如果我們無法成功適應這些演化中的產業、市場動態與消費者偏好，我們的營運與財務結果可能受到重大不利影響。此外，我們的競爭對手可能比我們更快或更有效地對產業與經濟條件及消費者行為的變化做出反應。為了保持競爭力，我們需要持續快速且正確地採用數位科技、建立分析能力並擴大品牌支出投資水平，而我們的競爭對手可能能更快且以更多資源實現此目標。在所有我們所處的市場中，競爭對手的激進行銷策略，如降低價格、品牌定位，以及增加資本或其他投資，都可能對我們的營運與財務結果造成重大不利影響。
